title: Seasonal Service Rider — Idle and Restore Terms of Electric Service by Rate Schedule
content:
A seasonal idle de-energizes a meter for the off season without closing the Electric Service by Rate Schedule account. The rider terms by schedule are:

| Term | R | RS | FH | GS-1 | GS-3 | IR | LP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Seasonal idle allowed | No | Yes | No | No | No | Yes | No |
| Calendar months idle before a restore is billed at the ordinary restore fee only | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 3 |
| Seasonal restore fee | $45.00 | $45.00 | $45.00 | $45.00 | $45.00 | $45.00 | $45.00 |
| Facility charge continues to bill during idle months | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |

Column key: R is Schedule R Residential Service; RS is Schedule RS Seasonal Residential Service; FH is Schedule FH Farm and Home Service; GS-1 is Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service; GS-3 is Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service; IR is Schedule IR Irrigation Service; LP is Schedule LP Large Power Service.

### Notes to the rider

- Only Schedule RS Seasonal Residential Service and Schedule IR Irrigation Service allow a seasonal idle; the idle figures listed for the other five schedules have no application.
- The minimum idle period is 3 calendar months on Schedule RS and 4 calendar months on Schedule IR.
- The seasonal restore fee is $45.00 on every schedule.
- On Schedule RS the facility charge keeps billing during idle months; on Schedule IR it does not.

### Hypothetical comparison

| Idle account (hypothetical) | Facility charge while idle | Minimum idle period |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule RS lake cabin | Continues ($38.75 per period) | 3 calendar months |
| Schedule IR pivot | Stops | 4 calendar months |
